comparator.name: Bachelor Computer Science and Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU/e's official 2026-2027 curriculum chart and current Education Guide, checked 2026-10-03, define a three-year, 180-EC programme for students starting in 2023-2024 or later. Year 1 contains twelve 5-EC components (60 EC), including ten computer-science and mathematics courses, an autonomous-systems CBL course and the first ITEC course. Year 2 contains eight 5-EC major courses, a 5-EC multidisciplinary CBL course and three 5-EC electives (60 EC). Year 3 contains one 5-EC capstone chosen from Heuristic Algorithms, Systems Integration or Software Development, a 10-EC Software Engineering project, a 10-EC individual Bachelor Final Project, the second 5-EC ITEC course and six 5-EC electives (60 EC). The nine freely chosen electives are retained as one 45-EC component rather than inventing a match-optimising package; the first-listed Heuristic Algorithms capstone provides the neutral representative capstone route.
components: Nine freely chosen 5-EC courses; maximum 15 EC at introductory level and minimum 15 EC at advanced level.
Neutral first-listed choice among the three current capstones; students take one capstone.
Group software-development project running over two quartiles.
Individual supervised research-oriented computer-science project and defended portfolio.

alternatives.label: Software, systems and algorithms
alternatives.concept: Builds a computer-science pathway around programming, software development, databases, networks and operating systems, algorithms, discrete mathematics, probability and selected AI methods. It is the closest feasible UCR response to TU/e CSE, while not reproducing TU/e's computer-systems architecture, automata and formal-languages, software-specification, technical-security and staged compulsory project sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum sustains programming, software, computer systems, algorithms and mathematical foundations across all three years.
progression: Programming, data and mathematical foundations precede databases, systems, software development, advanced algorithms and AI. Every prerequisite and planned 2026–29 term offering was checked in the current enriched workbook.

alternatives.label: AI, data and computational modelling
alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, algorithms and responsible computing while shifting the advanced programme toward linear algebra, numerical and systems modelling, probability, optimisation, machine learning and neural networks. It develops TU/e CSE's explicit AI, data and computational-modelling interests as a coherent second direction.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines a computing core with sustained mathematical modelling, statistics, optimisation and machine learning.
progression: Programming, database, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced algorithms, probability, optimisation, machine learning and neural networks. Every prerequisite and planned 2026–29 term offering was checked in the current enriched workbook.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, Research Methods & Statistics, business foundations, digital transformation, market research, linear systems, sociology and experimental methods replace product design, philosophy, networks and operating systems, software development, advanced algorithms, computer vision, reinforcement learning and AI decision-making. The 67.5-EC shift follows the evidenced AI/data/modelling emphasis and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor.

blocks: Introduction to Programming directly addresses programming fundamentals, with different language and project scope.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly addresses formal reasoning, set theory and discrete structures.
UCR combines logic and discrete mathematics in one selected course, which is aligned once rather than duplicated across two TU/e components.
Software Development addresses software design, implementation and testing, but not TU/e’s complete engineering sequence.
Algorithms & Data Structures directly addresses data structures and introductory algorithmic design.
Advanced Algorithms develops algorithm analysis and design beyond the introductory UCR course.
UCR has relevant logic and algorithms, but no selected course reproduces automata, formal languages and computability as one dedicated course.
UCR has software development but no separate selected course dedicated to formal software specification.
Computer systems, data management and security
UCR has no selected course dedicated to computer architecture and organisation.
Database Management Systems directly addresses data modelling, storage, authorisation and querying.
Networks & Operating Systems directly addresses network design and operation, with broader combined scope.
Networks & Operating Systems is already aligned to Networks and is not duplicated; TU/e has a separate operating-systems course.
AI Ethics addresses responsible computing but does not reproduce TU/e’s technical security course.
Mathematical Methods develops calculus-based methods used for computational modelling, with different breadth.
Linear Algebra directly addresses vectors, matrices and computational linear methods.
Research Methods & Statistics addresses statistical inference and empirical design, with less probability theory.
Introduction to Data Science addresses data collection, handling, analysis and visualisation, at a broader introductory level.
Machine Learning directly addresses supervised and unsupervised learning methods within TU/e’s combined statistics-and-ML component.
Human-centred design, communication and responsible technology
Ethics provides normative reasoning relevant to engineering ethics, but not TU/e’s technology-specific ITEC formation.
Academic formation, engineering projects and research
UCR has collaborative coursework but no selected 5-EC autonomous-systems challenge project.
UCR is interdisciplinary but does not reproduce TU/e’s dedicated multidisciplinary engineering challenge course.
TU/e preserves 45 EC of genuine elective choice; it is not treated as a fixed subject benchmark or filled with match-optimising inventions.
UCR advanced courses supply depth, but there is no selected integrated computer-science capstone equivalent.
UCR has no 10-EC compulsory group Software Engineering project.
TU/e requires a 10-EC individual research-oriented computer-science Bachelor Final Project; UCR optional independent research is shown separately by the compiler.
UCR ethics and social-science courses appear elsewhere, but no course is duplicated against this engineering-and-society component.

selection.assessment: The closest programme is a defensible 24-course response to TU/e's programming, software, algorithms, systems, mathematical and formal core. A second coherent curriculum follows the explicit AI, data and computational-modelling cluster and passes all feasibility and pairwise-distinctness rules. A human-centred computing direction was also tested to own the remaining direct programme interest, but the current UCR inventory does not contain enough distinct HCI, interaction-design and computer-systems courses to sustain a third 24-course computing programme without padding it with merely adjacent design, social-science or business courses.

notes.text: TU/e CSE includes dedicated Computer Systems, Automata and Formal Languages, Software Specification, Operating Systems, Security, autonomous-systems and multidisciplinary CBL courses, a compulsory 10-EC Software Engineering project, a choice of advanced capstone and a 10-EC individual research-oriented Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers substantial programming, databases, systems, algorithms, mathematics, data science and AI, but neither alternative reproduces that complete engineering and project sequence. TU/e also preserves 45 EC of genuine elective space.
